questions.problem: Evaluate the geometric series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{6}2(5)^{n-1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=2,$ $r=5$ and $N=6.$ If we substitute these values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{6}2(5)^{n-1} & =2\cdot \frac{(1-{5}^{6})}{1-5} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{(1-{5}^{6})}{(-4)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(-15\,624) \\  & =7\,812\end{aligned}
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{0}=24,r=\frac{1}{3}$ and $N=6$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{6} & =24\cdot \frac{[1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{6}]}{(1-\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =24\cdot \frac{[1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{6}]}{(\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =36\cdot (\frac{728}{729}) \\  & ≈35.951\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the final answer has been rounded to three decimal places.

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$

and therefore we can calculate the first term $a_1$ as follows:

$$

Notice that we can rewrite the series as follows:

$$
\sum_{n = 1}^{5} \dfrac{8}{2^{n-1}} = \sum_{n = 1}^{5} 8 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^{n-1}
$$

Since the above series is in the form $\displaystyle{\sum_{n=1}^N a_1 r^{n-1}},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum $S_N$ of a geometric series:

$$
S_N = a_1\dfrac{(1-r^N)}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $a_1 =8,$ $r = \dfrac{1}{2},$ and $N = 5.$ If we substitute these values into the above formula, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{5}\frac{8}{{2}^{n-1}} & =8\cdot \frac{[1-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{5}]}{(1-\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =8\cdot \frac{(\frac{31}{32})}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =8\cdot \frac{31}{16} \\  & =\frac{31}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Sum of a Geometric Series Given With a Zero Starting Index
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form $\displaystyle\sum{a_1 r^{n-1}},$ it is a geometric series. Notice that the index starts from $n=0$ instead of $n=1.$

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum $S_N$ of a geometric series:

$$
S_N = a_0\dfrac{(1-r^N)}{1-r}
$$

Note that we use $a_0$ in the sum formula because $a_0$ is the first term of the series.

In this case, $r =2.$ Also, note that $N=5,$ since there are $5$ terms in total: $a_0,$ $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
a_n = 3\left( 2\right)^{n-1},
$$

so the first term $a_0$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =3{(2)}^{0-1} \\  & =3{(2)}^{-1} \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

If we substitute $a_0 =\dfrac{3}{2},$ $r=2,$ and $N=5$ into the formula for $S_N,$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{5} & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{(1-{2}^{5})}{(1-2)} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{(-31)}{(-1)} \\  & =\frac{93}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
